# STM32H743 Nano FC + 4-in-1 80A ESC: System Design Package (Job #16)

## 0. Architectural Scope and Assumptions

**Architecture correction.** The STM32H743 is the **flight controller (FC)** MCU. It runs ArduPilot and generates bi-directional DShot600. The 48 kHz power-stage PWM is generated by **four separate ESC MCUs** (one per motor) running AM32 or BLHeli_32-class firmware, typically on AT32F421 or STM32G071 parts. The H743 does not commutate motors and should not do so: ArduPilot has no motor-commutation code, and four 6-step FOC/trapezoidal loops plus flight control on a single core would compromise both.

**Feasibility flag.** 80A per channel on a 20×20 mm "nano" ESC is only achievable as a **short burst (~1 s, all four channels)**. Section 3 derives this limit. Treat "80A" as a burst rating, never continuous.

**Design basis.** Where a part number is named, verify the parameters against its datasheet. All parameters below are representative values, not guaranteed specs.

| Parameter | Symbol | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Bus voltage (6S, max / nominal) | V_bus | 25.2 V / 22.2 V |
| MOSFET class | — | 60 V N-ch, PDFN 5×6 (40 V parts lack spike margin on 6S) |

## 1. Conduction Loss Model (80A Burst)

### 1.1 Current paths

In 6-step commutation, two phases conduct during each 60° sector.

- **ON interval (D):** current flows through HS(A), the motor, then LS(B).
- **OFF interval (1−D), synchronous freewheel:** current flows through LS(A), the motor, then LS(B).

In both intervals, exactly **two MOSFET channels** carry the full phase current I. The conduction loss per motor is therefore independent of duty cycle:

$$P_{cond,motor} = 2\,I^2\,R_{DS}(T_j)$$

$$R_{DS}(T_j) = R_{25}\left[1 + \alpha\,(T_j - 25)\right]$$

### 1.2 Evaluation at I = 80 A

| T_j | R_DS | P_cond per motor |
|---|---|---|
| 25 °C | 1.60 mΩ | 2·6400·1.6 m = **20.5 W** |
| 100 °C | 2.32 mΩ | **29.7 W** |
| 125 °C | 2.56 mΩ | **32.8 W** |

**Phase RMS current** (each phase conducts 2/3 of the electrical cycle):

$$I_{ph,rms} = 80\sqrt{2/3} = 65.3\ \text{A}$$

**Per-FET average.** Averaged over a full electrical revolution, the six FETs share the 2I²R loss:

$$P_{FET,avg} \approx \frac{I^2 R}{3} \approx 4.9\ \text{W
